slots.part: Enterprise · OAuth 2.0: roles, flows and PKCE

videos.oembed_title: An Illustrated Guide to OAuth and OpenID Connect
videos.watch_for: Learn the four OAuth roles, the authorization-code flow, scopes and consent, and how OpenID Connect adds an ID token on top. This also sets up Day 2.
videos.why_this_one: Okta's developer channel; a widely used illustrated explainer. The concepts are stable, so its age is fine.

videos.oembed_title: #PKCE explained - Proof Key for Code Exchange for #OAuth2 Authz Code Grant | Niko Köbler (@dasniko)
videos.channel: Niko Köbler - Expert for Keycloak IAM & SSO
videos.watch_for: See how code_verifier and code_challenge stop a stolen authorization code from being swapped for tokens. That is what PKCE adds to the code flow.
videos.why_this_one: Focused PKCE explainer from a well-known Keycloak/IAM expert. Not a big channel; length and date not verified.

videos.watch_for: Context as a budget: write, select, compress and isolate. The 'isolate' part explains why each agent in a team should see only its own slice.
videos.why_this_one: Lance Martin (LangChain) on the official LangChain channel. It covers the Anthropic vs Cognition trade-off from Day 1.

slots.part: Enterprise · OpenID Connect: ID tokens and what to check

videos.oembed_title: OpenID Connect - id_token, what they are, how they work
videos.watch_for: What an ID token is and which claims you check before trusting it (issuer, audience, expiry, signature). Then use the spec section as your checklist in code.
videos.why_this_one: Focused id_token explainer by an identity/API-security practitioner and author. A small channel; length and date not verified.
